subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: For macOS package updates that resolve to the already-installed version or leave stale `manualupdate` jobs, should OpenClaw short-circuit before stopping the service, add broader stale-job cleanup/dedupe, or preserve refresh behavior behind stronger handoff proof?
rationale: The source gap is real, but choosing the permanent update contract affects existing package refresh behavior, service restart expectations, and launchd cleanup scope.

options.title: Short-circuit and clean up stale jobs
options.body: Treat proven same-version package updates as no-op before service stop/restart, dedupe updater jobs, and extend cleanup to the observed `manualupdate` family with live macOS proof.

options.title: Durable refresh contract
options.body: Keep package refresh behavior but require a stronger launchd handoff that proves service health, stale-job cleanup, and local node recovery after every refresh.

options.title: Split trackers first
options.body: Move node-skew, no-op update policy, and stale updater cleanup into separate owner-approved issues before allowing implementation.

recommendation.title: Short-circuit and clean up stale jobs
recommendation.body: Treat proven same-version package updates as no-op before service stop/restart, dedupe updater jobs, and extend cleanup to the observed `manualupdate` family with live macOS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has recent package service-state cutover history and repository-member direction on adjacent macOS update launchd trackers.
